headline: Awarded red light camera contract to Sitestream LLC; recommended Centre Square land sales to Carrier Construction Inc.
summary: Several residents urged the council not to award the red light camera contract before it voted 6-1 to do so. The council also created a Charter Revision Commission and adopted a Vision Zero goal of eliminating roadway deaths and serious injuries by 2046. Starting November 1, 2026, the city will not accept applications for new smoke and vape shops.
decisions: Confirmed board and commission appointments by voice vote.
Adopted 25 consent calendar items in one unanimous vote.
Approved $90,408.79 in tax refunds.
Accepted a $3,150,000 HUD award for preconstruction at the Bristol ASHER/CPAT facility and referred the matter to the Board of Finance.
Referred the possible sale of Lot #6 in the Southeast Bristol Business Park for required planning and public hearing steps.
Approved a $30,500 engineering amendment for the Andrews Street culvert, raising the contract to $222,800.
Approved a $38,500 engineering amendment for the Mellen Street culvert, raising the contract to $171,817.36.
Approved Amendment No. 3, adding $95,824.97 to the Beals Community Center renovation contract.
Approved a $330,700 amendment to the Page Park design contract, for a revised total of $2,190,190.00.
Awarded the update of the 2018 Plan of Conservation and Development to IMEG Corp. for $153,500.
Placed on file several positive planning referrals for city land sales and purchases.
Accepted a 7.5-acre open space donation on Perkins Street from the Clinton S. Roberts Foundation, conditioned on an appraisal.
Accepted an offer from Accurate Mechanical LLC to buy 81 Church Avenue for $211,000.
Authorized use of 30 Cross Street as a joint regional training facility for the Fire and Police Departments.
Created a seven-member Charter Revision Commission, with a draft report due May 28, 2027, by a 7-0 roll call vote.
Approved renewing the Bristol-Burlington Health District lease at the Beals Senior Community Center for one year, at $121,857.30 per year plus a heating surcharge.
Adopted amendments to the traffic ordinance on red light cameras, removing speed camera references, by a 6-1 vote.
Awarded the three-year red light traffic safety camera contract to Sitestream LLC, by a 6-1 vote.
Placed on record a Zoning Commission motion for a moratorium on new smoke and vape shops, effective November 1, 2026.
Approved amending the Edgewood Pre-K Academy renovation contract by $28,217,964.12, bringing the guaranteed maximum price to $29,873,359.
Adopted a Senior Volunteer Tax Relief Program offering up to a $300 annual property tax credit for volunteering, by a 7-0 roll call vote.
Adopted a Vision Zero resolution with a goal of eliminating roadway deaths and serious injuries by 2046, by a 7-0 roll call vote.
Approved a resolution letting the mayor extend the Pequabuck River Trail state grant by six months, with no added funds.
Approved a resolution letting the mayor extend the flood resilience plan state grant by three months, with no added funds.
Recommended selling Centre Square North Main Street parcel 30-1 to Carrier Construction Inc. for $1, with an Enterprise Zone tax abatement schedule.
Recommended selling Centre Square North Main Street parcel 30-3 to Carrier Construction Inc. for $250,000 for a mixed-use development.

546 
OCTOBER 13, 2026 
 
The regular meeting of the City Council was held on Tuesday, October 13, 2026 in the City 
Hall Council Chambers, 111 North Main Street at 7:08 p.m. Present: Mayor Zoppo-Sassu; Council 
Members Dickau, Hahn, Kelley, Rosengren, Seymour and Tyler. 
  
1. CALL TO ORDER 
 
 U.S. Marine Corps. Veteran Joseph Caminiti was recognized for this 102nd birthday.  John 
Lodovico, Veterans Affairs Liaison to the Council spoke about Mr. Caminiti’s heroic actions during 
his service in World War II.  Mr. Caminiti stormed the beaches of Iwo Jima, saved numerous 
servicemen’s lives in the process, and helped liberate Guam.  Mayor Zoppo-Sassu presented him with 
an official Congressional Record which was entered into the record of the 119th United States 
Congress, second session, by Representative John Larson and the House of Representatives.   
 
 Ryan Cook and DJ Green were recognized for their achievements in the Special Olympics.  
DJ won his preliminaries, then placed 7th in the 1500m, 5th in the 400m, and 5th in the relay.  Ryan 
brought home gold medals in team bowling and males doubles, and 6th in singles.  They have 
represented Bristol in the Special Olympics since 2024.   
 
 Bristol Girls Little League Junior Softball Team was recognized for winning the Connecticut 
State Title and advancing to the East Regional playoffs in Pennsylvania.  The team consisted of:  
Layla Annino, Zoey Comandini, Madisyn Daigle, Ellie Hudson, Tilly Kelly, Dreah LaJoie, Alaina 
Lefurgey, Kylie Nass, Ava Theriault, Kamden Treannie, Makenzie Wentland, Victoria Zaldivar; and  
Kyle Wentland – Manager, Bryan Theriault – Coach, and Jon Hudson – Coach. 
 
 Bristol Girls Little League 12U All-Stars Softball Team was recognized for winning the East 
Regional Title and representing Bristol in the Little League World Series hosted in Greenville, North 
Carolina.  The team consisted of:  Lucy Bastiaanse, Keeva Knowles, Lucy Kalat, Ava Lefurgey, 
Makinnley Whitlock, Mary Thompson, Avery Collins, Dakota Green, Ellie Tiscia, FaithMarie Soto, 
Alex Patterson, Juliana Pavlak; and Adam Whitlock – Manager, Kevina Kalat – Coach, and Mike 
Bastiaanse – Coach.  
   
2. APPROVAL OF MINUTES 
 
On motion of Council Member Rosengren and seconded by Council Member Dickau, it was 
unanimously voted:  To approve the minutes of the special City Council meeting held on September 3, 
2026, the regular meeting held on September 8, 2026, and the special meeting held on September 22, 
2026. 
   
3. PUBLIC PARTICIPATION  
  
 Jasmine Anthony, Candidate for Kid Governor, spoke about her recycling platform. 
 
 Victor Lagace, 117 Broad St. – Mr. Lagace spoke about the ongoing water problem behind 
his building.  He believes it is due to a lack of storm drains. 
 
 Mark Vose, 92 Bingham St.– Mr. Vose spoke about the same water problem and described 
going out in the middle of the night during rainstorms to clean the storm drains to keep his property 
from flooding.
547 
OCTOBER 13, 2026 
 
 Shelly Mastroianni, 120 Sixth St. - Ms. Mastroianni asked who is going to pay the cost of 
digging the holes for the poles for the red light cameras at each intersection.  She expressed that law 
enforcement should be the only entity entitled to look for identifying information and that there 
should be a way to pay for a violation without having to pay a processing fee. 
 
 Gabby Carrano, 70 Seneca Rd. – Ms. Carrano asked the Council if their decisions regarding 
the red light cameras represents the thoughts of their constituents and urged the Council not to award 
the red light traffic camera contract to a vendor. 
 
 Brian Whitford, 27 Sigourney St. – Mr. Whitford described receiving fines and tickets for 
one of his vehicles that was parked in his garage on the dates of the supposed toll offenses that took 
place in New York.  He wanted to show that mistakes can happen with cameras and cause a lot of 
frustration for innocent residents.  
 
 Nick Palmer, 69 Cronin St. – Mr. Palmer requested a surveillance oversight ordinance and 
also implored the Council not to award the red light traffic camera contract.

unanimously voted:  To move agenda items #9 Resignations and #10 Appointments to this point on

Connecticut General Statutes, the City Council of the City of Bristol hereby creates a

hold any other public office in this City and not more than a bare majority of whom shall 
be members of any one political party.  Said Commission is hereby directed to make its

 Communication received from Public Works Director Rogozinski. 
 
 On motion of Council Member Rosengren and seconded by Council Member Dickau, it

 On motion of Council Member Tyler and seconded by Council Member Dickau, it was 
unanimously voted:  To approve a resolution implementing the Vision Zero Initiative in Support 
of Safe, Healthy and Equitable Mobility, establishing a goal of eliminating roadway fatalities and 
serious injuries on City of Bristol streets by 2046 and supporting the City's participation in the 
Vision Zero / Safe Streets and Roads for All Safety Action Plan being prepared by NVCOG. 
 
The Resolution reads as follows –  
WHEREAS, safe, healthy and equitable mobility is a foundation of our community; and  
WHEREAS, public streets and rights of way connect our neighborhoods into one City of Bristol; and  
WHEREAS, the City Council is concerned about roadway accidents and serious injuries on City of 
Bristol streets and state roads; and   
WHEREAS, there has been a rise in traffic-related fatalities and serious injuries in Connecticut and 
across the United States;
559 
OCTOBER 13, 2026 
 
WHEREAS, our community must come together and increase efforts to create safer and more welcoming 
streets for all; and  
WHEREAS, proven measures exist to reduce the number of crashes on our streets with a thoughtful and 
data-backed mix of equitable transportation engineering, enforcement, and education; and  
WHEREAS, roadway designs focused on the Complete streets concept to prioritize reducing vehicular 
speeding, improve and expand pedestrian and bicycle facilities, and create safer streets for all users; and  
WHEREAS, speeding, red light running, ignoring traffic signals and signs, and distracted driving are 
among the leading causes of motor vehicle crashes; and  
WHEREAS, the City of Bristol has already achieved significant gains in traffic safety; and  
WHEREAS, Vision Zero is a goal to achieve zero roadway deaths and serious injuries on our streets and 
adjacent rights of way; and  
WHEREAS, Vision Zero goals have been adopted by other municipalities and states around the country, 
and recently by the federal government; and  
WHEREAS, Vision Zero is premised on the fundamental principal that loss of life and serious injury 
from traffic crashes is unacceptable, yet acknowledges that while people make mistakes, our roadway 
network should be designed to ensure those inevitable mistakes do not result in severe injuries or deaths; 
and 
WHEREAS, for Vision Zero to be accepted, it must be thoughtfully integrated into and embraced by 
multiple stakeholders, including traffic engineers, police and emergency services, City government 
leaders, the business community, neighborhood and community groups, and the public at large.  
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL THAT: 
1. The City of Bristol supports the five principles of the Vision Zero Initiative, namely that: 
a. Deaths and serious injuries caused by traffic crashes are preventable; 
b. Human life and health should be prioritized in all transportation systems and in all 
aspects of transportation planning and design; 
c. Human error is inevitable and transportation systems should be forgiving; 
d. Transportation planning should focus on system-level changes to influence all 
individual’s behavior; and  
e. Speed is highly important factor in crash severity. 
2. Adoption of a Vision Zero Initiative tailored to the City of Bristol. City Departments are 
hereby directed to adopt the Vision Zero Initiative in the City of Bristol with the goal of 
eliminated fatalities and severe injuries on City of Bristol streets by 2046.  
 
3. Establishment of Task Force. In support of the Vision Zero Initiative, the mayor shall establish 
a Vision Zero Task Force committee that shall be composed Department of Public Works, Police 
Department, Community Services, Board of Public Works, and Senior Center, with additional 
representatives added as appropriate.

Works, or its committees, on the findings and progress of the Vision Zero Task Force Committee,
